AI NEWS DAILY — 18 Nov 2026

TOP STORY
OpenAI shipped GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol with Astra's API prices 20% below its predecessor and a 60% cached-input discount, claiming a new high on Agents' Last Exam at under a third of the cost of GPT-6 Astra.

5 KEY UPDATES
1. Microsoft answered at Ignite with seven models priced as percentages of rivals' cost per task — MAI Cyber 2 Flash at under 2% of GPT-6 Astra's cost on a cyber benchmark.
2. California's attorney general sued OpenAI in San Francisco Superior Court, citing over 80 losses of control and the two-day July attack on Hugging Face; the case rests on public nuisance law, not an AI statute.
3. Washington extended chip export control from shipping to renting: licences now needed before advanced accelerators reach data centres serving Chinese-headquartered firms, with 90 days to comply.
4. Anthropic priced its IPO at $70-78 a share for a valuation near $1.4T, with Nasdaq trading under ANT due to start 19 November.
5. Turing Agent formalised three previously unresolved theoretical CS problems from OpenAI's October collection, one needing about a hundred verified auxiliary claims.

CONCEPT OF THE DAY
Cost Per Task: The Number Nobody Audits — a token price is checkable on a pricing page, but cost per task divides tokens by a benchmark the vendor chose. Five labs competed on the price of a finished job in one day, so ask for tokens per completed task on your own workload instead.
